selected_passages.title: sources/SBF_s_trial_starts_soon_but_how_did_he_and_FTX_get_here
selected_passages.text: Sam Bankman-Fried's criminal trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy against FTX has begun, following the exchange's collapse in November 2022 due to severe liquidity issues and mismanagement of customer funds. The once-valued $32 billion crypto empire filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, leading to the arrest of Bankman-Fried and the guilty pleas of former executives Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison, while the trial proceeds with high-profile legal representation.

The text contrasts SBF's positive media coverage and perceived idealism with public outrage over the financial fraud, noting his political maneuvering and the subsequent crash of cryptocurrency valuations on the platform.

selected_passages.text: Shortly afterward, as the trial neared late afternoon, the government called Adam Yedidia to the stand. A fast-talking graduate of MIT, he and Bankman-Fried were close friends in college, he said. And after Bankman-Fried left Jane Street, the high-frequency trading firm where the former billionaire got his start in finance after MIT, he persuaded Yedidia to join him as a trader at Alameda and then as a developer at FTX.
